data.body:
CLOSING — change 1344 MERGED as 929ba5d66940549857fb5232082bebe94e45d59c (LLM-Review +1,
Verified +1, submitted). All 7 criteria verified against the MERGED tree, several by live
measurement rather than by reading. Evidence per criterion:

AC1 — "whether Bedrock's Converse API can carry Anthropic's server-side web_search is MEASURED
and recorded, with the call and its outcome."
MEASURED LIVE against the merged code, both arms, with the Anthropic arm as the control:
    BedrockProvider(region_name="us-east-1").model_profile("us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8")
      supported_native_tools = frozenset()          <- EMPTY
      -> native_web_search=False -> route(web=True) = "local"
    AnthropicProvider().model_profile("claude-opus-4-8")
      supported_native_tools = frozenset({WebSearchTool, MCPServerTool, CodeExecutionTool,
                                          MemoryTool, WebFetchTool, ToolSearchTool})
      -> native_web_search=True  -> route(web=True) = "native"
ANSWER: Bedrock does NOT carry the server-side tool, so T1 is served there by the LOCAL route.
The answer is read from `supported_native_tools` — the same registry pydantic-ai itself filters
against — so it cannot drift from what actually happens at request time.

AC2 — "T1 has WEB ACCESS ON EVERY PROVIDER rebar can route it to, including Bedrock — verified by
a run on each configured provider, not by inspection of the gate condition."
Two independent legs, neither of which inspects the gate condition:
  * PER-PROVIDER RUNS through the real runner:
    `test_runner_attaches_web_capability_on_every_provider` is parametrized over
    anthropic / bedrock / openai / google-gla. Each case builds the REAL model+provider (only the
    Agent class is doubled), drives PydanticAIRunner.run(), captures the Agent construction kwargs
    and asserts a WebSearch capability is present with `get_native_tools()` non-empty and
    `get_toolset() is not None`. These now pass in GITHUB CI on all four matrix legs
    (ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 + macos 3.13) — i.e. in an environment with no AWS config and no
    provider credentials, so the result is not an artifact of this host.
  * PER-PROVIDER ROUTE derived from each provider's REAL profile — the live measurement in AC1.
RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: no live MODEL CALL was made on each provider (that
would be four paid runs and, for T1 specifically, requires a plan whose content actually trips
T1's overlay triggers). A plan review executed on this ticket today took the fast structural path
(`claim_path: "no-llm/no-network"`), so T1 did not run in it and its verdict honestly recorded
`web_access: "off"` — which is itself the AC5 mechanism working.

AC3 — "the web-access decision no longer consults a provider-name prefix; it derives from the
model profile / capability registry … the attested guard is NOT weakened."
`capabilities.web_search_capabilities(*, web: bool)` — keyword-only, and takes NO model or
provider argument at all, so it is structurally incapable of gating on a name shape.
`_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` (the `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` site) is DELETED.
`native_web_search` is set by `_supports_native_web_search(profile)` (capabilities.py:130, used at
:351) — membership in `supported_native_tools`, never a prefix. The attested guard
`test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is present and untouched at
tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:119 and passes in the full suite.

AC4 — "if a rebar-side mechanism is required for any provider, the egress / caching /
prompt-injection-from-fetched-content tradeoff … is addressed explicitly, not bypassed."
Argued in a block comment above `web_search_capabilities` (capabilities.py:161-189), in the code
where the decision lives rather than only in a ticket: fetched text is named UNTRUSTED INPUT to a
BLOCKING gate; VOLUME is bounded on both routes (native max_uses=5 per run, local max_results=5
per call, plus the agentic loop's own budget); SHAPE is bounded on the local route because the
DuckDuckGo tool returns title+href+snippet only, never page bodies — so this is a SEARCH
capability and no rebar-side HTTP fetcher was written, which is the specific thing the original
provider-side-only design was protecting; AUTHORITY is bounded downstream by the findings contract
plus a T1 rubric clause naming results untrusted data. DOMAIN CONTROLS are deliberately NOT used
and the reason is recorded as a tradeoff: an allowlist is self-defeating for a criterion whose job
is finding UNKNOWN prior art, and a blocklist cannot hold uniformly — at capability level it kills
the local fallback (see below), at native-instance level it binds one route only, and a control
that holds on one route but not the other is misleading.

AC5 — "a signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities` records that web access WAS attached,
so a future silent withdrawal is impossible to miss."
`web_access_provenance(caps, *, web)` (capabilities.py:522) returns `"native" | "local" | "off"`,
threaded into `provenance_for(...)["capabilities"]["web_access"]`. Three values not a boolean,
because only `"local"` means third-party text entered rebar's process. Confirmed populated on a
REAL verdict today: a live Bedrock `rebar review-plan` on this ticket emitted
    provider_provenance: {provider: bedrock, model: bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6,
                          endpoint_host: null, tier: first_class,
                          capabilities: {..., web_access: "off"}}
`"off"` is correct there — that run never attached the capability — and it is exactly the property
the AC asks for: the run's web state is now legible in the verdict, so the silent case that hid
this bug through the whole Bedrock cutover cannot recur.

AC6 — "`plan_review_T1.md` no longer describes web access as provider-dependent or optional, while
still forbidding fabricated citations."
Verified on the merged file: zero matches for "may be offered", "provider-dependent", or "when it
is not available". The anti-fabrication clause is retained and strengthened ("cite only sources you
actually retrieved"), plus a new clause naming results untrusted data rather than instructions.

AC7 — "tests pin the above and are each verified RED by mutation, including one that fails if the
capability is withheld on a `bedrock:`-qualified model."
tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py, 20 tests, each family verified RED by mutation (recorded in
the implementation comment above): reinstating the anthropic prefix gate -> 5 RED including the
bedrock parametrization; deleting the provenance field -> RED `KeyError: 'web_access'`; attaching
on web=False -> 4 RED on the byte-identical assertion; reverting the T1 rubric -> RED. Whole suite
green at the merged tree: 9924 passed, 34 skipped, 0 failed.

THE TRAP THAT MUST NOT BE UNDONE, re-verified live today: `max_uses`/`blocked_domains`/
`allowed_domains` set at the CAPABILITY level flip pydantic-ai's `_requires_native()` True, and
`NativeOrLocalTool.get_toolset()` then returns None — suppressing the local fallback and
re-creating this exact bug on any provider without the native tool. They therefore ride the NATIVE
TOOL INSTANCE. Confirmed today on the merged code: `web_search_capabilities(web=True)[0]` is a
`WebSearch` whose `get_toolset() is not None` is True, and `web_search_capabilities(web=False)` is
None.

A NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS NEXT — the two CI failures on this change were NOT a code defect and
NOT the stale-base trap. They were a host-dependence in my own new test: the bedrock leg builds a
real provider, which resolves BOTH a region AND credentials, and this host had both while CI had
neither. Fixed test-only by pinning `bedrock_region_name` on the LLMConfig FIELD (the env var
REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION is read only by the env/table factory, never by direct construction) plus
placeholder AWS creds to short-circuit the IMDS lookup that otherwise trips the network-forbidden
fixture. Verified in a stripped CI simulation and on this host: 20 passed both ways.
